name: 1623 Prairie Avenue — Granger Farwell's stone-front house with its carved oriel, K01 frontage assembly

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling (D), the middle unit of the group'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: T-2433 (piece 2 of T-1869) refines the district draft (T-2335) in place under the same id. Which number Farwell's house stood at is argued in docs/RESEARCH/k01-1623-farwell-2433/README.md: 1623, the north neighbour of Hugh J. McBirney's 1625 (the 1890 Inland Architect photograph of 1625 shows Farwell's oriel and arched entrance against its north wall), the 1885 permits' '1625' being the numbering of before McBirney built. The front is built from the house's one drawing, Treat & Foltz's plate in The Building Budget (June 188-, probably 1886; building_budget_1886_06_hamline_farwell_houses, the right-hand house), read against the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20, which controls the plan: a K02 stone street front with a rusticated base on K03 brick sides and rear, the drawing's canted oriel on K08's corbelled oriel across the second storey with its mullioned and transomed lights, the door in the south bay at the head of a K07 stoop and the window in the north bay over a basement light, a K10 cornice and a slated K04/K05 hip with a tall stack against the north wall. What the drawing shows and K01 does not yet build — the two round arches at grade, the oriel's carved frieze, its upper stage of lights and its steep conical roof rising through the eave, the iron-grilled basement arch and the stoop's rails — is listed open in its match record (data/reference_views/house_1623_prairie/building_budget_front.match.json) for T-2435. Everything not read is reconstructed and recorded as L-k01-1623-farwell-oriel-front-2433. T-2728 (piece 1 of T-2435) builds the entrance's deep round arch, the stoop's iron rails, the basement light's grille and the rock-faced front from the drawing (L-k01-1623-farwell-entrance-2728); what still differs is open in the match record for T-2729. T-2818 (piece 2 of T-2779) lays the drawing's broad segmental basement light behind its scrolled grille.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 1623 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1623 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).
position.note: The rear corner of the K01 main body at its north (low-v) side, the draft's own origin (lot frame u 18.000, v -2.500 m from the middle of the rear lot line), which already stands on the 1911 sheet's traced main part (s20fp-1623-b1), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.604 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line, so v runs south.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s20fp-1623-b1) in the lot frame: the street front's face at u 37.5 m from the rear lot line's middle, the rear wall at 18.0, the south wall at v 3.7 (the party wall with 1625) and the north wall at -2.5, where the trace's front part stands, so 19.5 m deep and 6.2 m along the front. Behind u 33 the trace widens 1.1 m north to the party wall with 1621 (v -3.6) and is notched there for the light well the two houses share; that strip and the notch are not built.

stories.note: Two full storeys over a raised basement, and a third in the roof, lit by the oriel's upper stage under its cone: the Building Budget drawing's own count (the raised basement with its grilled light; the principal storey of the two arches; the second storey, the oriel's lower stage of tall transomed lights; above its carved frieze the oriel's upper stage of short lights rising past the main cornice into the roof). The 1911 sheet prints '3B' over the house, three storeys and a basement, which the drawing's count agrees with when its roof storey is counted (docs/RESEARCH/k01-1623-farwell-2433/README.md).

construction.note: The drawing draws the street front in stone, rock-faced and rusticated in big blocks about the arches and in the basement, and the side walls not at all; the 1911 sheet's register reads the group as brick and records no stone front for 1623. A stone front laid on brick is read from the house's one picture, the sheet's silence noted: it may not colour a front it draws inside an attached group, and a photograph after 1886 settles it.

principal_floor_m.note: 1.85 m over grade, read through the drawing's camera (data/reference_views/house_1623_prairie/building_budget_front.json): the stoop's head at the door and the arched window's sill, about 1.85 and 2.1 m at the front's 46 px/m, good to about 10 %. Just above the contract's 0.8-1.8 m starting range, so it stands on the drawing.

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor, principal storey first: 3.9 m, so the second floor lands at the oriel's sill (about 5.8 m through the camera), and 4.0 m, so the wall head stands at 9.75 m, at the main cornice the drawing draws south of the oriel (about 9.7 m). No dimension is printed on the drawing.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone front on its brick backing, as 1612's, 1619's and 1634's.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A brick-and-a-half wall, as every K01 brick house's.

service_wall_brick.note: The one K03 panel k03_brick lays.

stone_front.note: The drawing draws the front's base in big rock-faced blocks, coursed and rusticated up to the arches' springing, and the oriel in dressed stone; it is monochrome, so the stone is chosen: K02's buff Lemont limestone, the common Chicago building stone of the 1880s, over two rusticated base courses (the most its K02 profile lays). T-2728 lays it rock-faced (`dressing`, the profile's 0-0.025 m face), as the drawing draws every block from grade to the arches' springing. T-2819: above the carved band at the arches' springing the drawing draws the narrow strips beside the oriel as smoother coursed stone, ruled in level courses with few marks on their faces, where every block under it is drawn rock-faced. So K01 lays the front evenly (`coursing`, rhythm `even`: no high and low courses) with the profile's whole 0-0.025 m rock face under 3.4 m, the band's top (street_front_dress.carved_band), and a fifth of it (0-0.005 m) above, so the stone over the band reads smoother and still quarry-faced. The share is reconstructed: the drawing draws the difference, not its depth (L-k01-1623-farwell-entrance-2728). Replaceable by any description naming the stone.

wall_head.note: K10's bracketed cornice, the nearest the kit comes to the drawing's moulded cornice with its row of small blocks, which the drawing shows south of the oriel at about 9.7 m.

roof_form.note: A pitched roof: the drawing slates a steep roof behind the oriel's cone, its slope showing south of it; K01's hip is the honest stand-in, the cone the oriel carries through the eave being T-2435's.

roof_pitch_deg.note: 45 degrees, the K01 contract's steepest hip: the drawing's slope behind the cone rises to about 12.7 m through the camera, which a 45-degree hip over the 6.2 m front reaches at its ridge (12.85 m).

stair_tread_m.note: The K07 contract's shortest tread, so the stoop's eleven risers and its landing stay inside the 3.8 m front yard; the drawing's stoop runs straight up from the walk to the door.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A 0.9 m landing before the door, so the stoop stays inside the 3.8 m front yard.

stoop_width_m.note: The drawing's stoop between its iron rails and newels, about 1.7 m across at the front's scale.

entrance_bay.note: The door is in the front's south bay: the drawing puts the entrance arch, up its stoop, at the right of the front, south of the arched window. K01 lays a front of named openings (street_front_openings) as three bays entered in the middle one, so the front is laid as the window's bay, the door's, and a narrow blank third bay at the south corner, which holds no opening.

front_bays.note: Read through the drawing's camera and scaled to the sheet's 6.2 m front (the drawing's front is about 6.5 m): the arched window's centre at about 1.55 m from the north wall and the entrance arch's at about 4.6 m, both built there (T-2777): the oriel over them stands on its corbelling clear of both arches' heads, so it no longer needs the width between their centres. The third, at 5.7 m, is the blank bay K01's named-opening front needs (entrance_bay). T-2817: the entrance arch's centre moved to 4.55 m, 0.05 m north, so that its broader ring (the arch now 1.85 m across) stays a course inside the south corner; the drawn arch's intrados centres at about x 257, the built one at about x 252.

windows.why_not_ordinary: a mullioned oriel's light, four to its 3.4 m front between stone mullions, as narrow as the drawing's (about 0.6 m, at its 0.82 m pitch)
a light in each of the oriel's cants, as the drawing's, narrowed and set toward the cant's front end so its recess stays in front of the house wall
the upper stage's shorter lights, four to the oriel's 3.4 m front over the four below, as narrow as the drawing's
a light in each of the upper stage's cants, as the drawing's, narrowed and set at the cant's front end, so its sill stands clear over where the house's eave and gutter die into the cant

bays.note: The drawing's canted oriel, read through its camera: centred on the front, about 4.8 m across where its cants meet the wall and 3.4 m of front, standing on corbelling over the two arches from about 4.9 m, its sill at the second floor (about 5.8 m), four tall transomed lights across its front and one in each cant, then a carved frieze at about 8.1-9.0 m and an upper stage of short lights under a steep conical roof whose eave stands at about 10.9 m. T-2777 builds the K08 kit's canted corbelled oriel at the drawing's size, centred at 3.1 m: 4.8 m at the wall and 3.4 m of front, over the window and the entrance arch, whose heads (4.4 and 4.55 m) stand more than 0.3 m under its lowest corbel course (4.95 m), so neither is behind it (T-2541's rule). Its depth is 0.65 m, cants at about 43 degrees: the drawing's level, square-on camera cannot read the depth (between 0.65 and 0.9 m out the oriel's front moves under 3 px in it, inside the camera's residuals), and four 0.2 m corbel courses, which fit between the second floor and the entrance's head, carry at most 0.65 m under the kit's oversail rule (0.65 of a course's height a course), so the depth is the most the drawn corbelling carries (inferred). K06 transomed lights: four 0.55 m across to its front at 0.82 m centres (the drawing's about 0.6 m at about 0.83 m), and a 0.35 m light in each cant set toward its front end, the most a 0.96 m cant holds with its recess kept in front of the house wall (the drawing's cant lights read wider); the build before had three to the front and blind cheeks. T-2778 carries it up through the main eave as the drawing does, its heights read through the drawing's camera at the oriel's front (about 47.5 px/m): the second storey to a string course at 8.35 m (the drawing's lower lights about 6.05-8.2 m, built 6.03-8.03 m), the carved frieze between two string courses from 8.35 to 9.5 m (drawn about 8.45-9.4 m, rows 247-292), the upper stage to 10.9 m with four shorter lights to its front and one in each cant (drawn about 9.6-10.7 m, rows 186-237, built 9.69-10.69 m; five read in the drawing, the north cant's foreshortened to a sliver, as it is through the camera), its cornice at about 11.15 m (row about 165) and a steep slate spire over it, every plane rising from its eaves to one apex at about 13.85 m (row about 52) under a finial; the drawing's hips stand at the oriel's corners, so the cone is a polygonal one (`through_eave`, k01_frontage_params._bays). The ticket's figures (frieze 8.1-9.0 m, upper stage to 10.4 m, eave 10.9 m, apex 13.4 m) read about 0.35 m low through this camera, which puts the house's own cornice at 9.7 m within about 3 px; the build follows the camera. The house's eave, its gutter and its bed moulding die into the oriel's cants, and its back is closed in its stone over the wall head (9.75 m) to the apex, where no wall stands behind it. The cant lights are 0.3 m and stand at each cant's front end, so their sills clear the house's eave and gutter where those meet the cant (the drawing's read a little wider). Reconstructed: the frieze's carving, which the drawing draws as interlaced strapwork in a sunk panel on each face, is a dressed panel on each face carrying a guilloche of interlaced rings (L-k01-1623-farwell-oriel-front-2433); the eaves' 0.15 m overhang and 0.25 m fascia; the spire's slate and the kit's turned finial.

side_bays.note: No windows in the north side wall: it is a party wall with 1621 on the 1911 sheet, and the light well the two houses share is not built.

north_bays.note: No windows in the south side wall (K01's high-v 'north'): a party wall with 1625 on the 1911 sheet.

rear_bays.note: Two windows a storey in the rear wall, the front's two bays; no picture shows the rear.

sash_by_storey.note: The rear wall's sash, a storey each; the street front's openings are named in street_front_openings and its second storey is the oriel's. No picture shows the rear.

roof_covering.note: The drawing slates the roof and the cone; Pennsylvania slate with copper flashing and ridge roll, as 1619's.

chimneys.note: The drawing's tall stack rises against the north wall just behind the front, its top at about 13 m through the camera, stepped in its height; built as K15's plain stack 2.9 m behind the front on the north party wall, with a second over the rear rooms. Its steps are not built.

rainwater.note: Copper half-round gutters and two pipes by the front's corners. The drawing draws no pipe down its front, so T-2819 hangs them on the flanks 0.35 m back from the front's corners, as 1625's photograph hangs its pipe (T-2753), where until then they ran down the front's face at its corners, as 1619's; where the pipes stand is reconstructed, the drawing showing neither flank.

window_kit.note: K06's two-over-two sash in the side and rear walls; under the principal storey's arch its wide sash with the head glazed as a lattice of square lights, as the drawing draws it (T-2819, k06.opening.sash_round_lattice_wide; until then the radial fanlight of 1612's), and under that (T-2818) its broad segmental basement light, the drawing's low arched opening.

entrance_kit.note: T-2728: the drawing's entrance is a deep round arch beside the window's and matching it, its door standing at the back of a recess whose lit south jamb shows inside the arch, a glazed door under a carved light. Built as K07's deep-arch entrance: round it the front's stone cut into a ring of long voussoirs under the window's keystone, with a curved extrados standing 0.04 m before the wall (`arch`, as 1621's, T-2531); and the door 0.95 m back, K07's own reveal for the variant, whose vestibule carries the recess past the 0.45 m front (`reveal_depth_m`). The stoop climbs between iron rails and newels, not stone cheeks (`cheeks` false; the rails are street_front_dress.stoop_rails), 3.8 m of front yard to the 1904 parcel's street line. Read from the drawing: the arch, its place and the recess; reconstructed (the value's grade, since most of the entrance's joinery is the kit's): the leaves (K07's panelled pair under a radial fanlight, where the drawing half-hides a glazed door under a carved light in the recess's shadow), the ring's projection and the recess's depth (L-k01-1623-farwell-entrance-2728). T-2817: the arch is the porch's mouth, as broad as the window's: read through the drawing's camera at the front's 46 px/m, its intrados stands between x 215 and 300 (about 1.85 m), its jambs rise to the carved band at about y 535 (about 3.4 m) and its crown at about y 482 (about 4.55 m), so the drawn arch is a little stilted; built round at 1.85 m (`opening_m`), 2.6 m to its crown over the principal floor, so it springs at 3.525 m and its crown stands at 4.45 m, splitting the drawn springing and crown, under its 0.45 m ring, whose top (4.9 m) stands about 5 px under the drawn ring's (about y 460, 5.0 m): a deeper ring would run within a course of the south corner. At the porch's back (`porch_door`), 0.95 m in, a wall closes the arch round the door's own opening, 1.0 m across under a flat head 2.2 m up, its centre 0.1 m north of the arch's axis (v 4.45): the drawing draws the door's frame between x 222 and 262 at the porch's back (43.9 px/m there), about v 4.0-4.9, and the back wall lit south of it to the arch's south jamb, which is the 'lit south jamb' of T-2728's reading. A single leaf, glazed above its lock rail as the drawing's glazed door with its curtain, under a 0.45 m transom in place of the drawing's carved light. The stoop stands north of the arch (`stoop_v_m` 3.5): the drawing's rails' head newels centre at about x 225 (v 3.9 at the landing's edge) and their foot newels at about x 200 (v 3.15 at the foot), the drawn flight a little skewed in the pen perspective; 3.5 m splits them, 1.05 m north of the arch's axis, where the ticket's figure (about 1.3 m) was read off the rails' 60 px at the front's own scale, too small for the foot's. Its landing runs on south past the arch to the front's south wall as a stone terrace at the principal floor (`terrace` right, to v 6.2), which carries the porch's mouth, and the drawing's iron guard stands along it (street_front_dress.stoop_rails.guard). Reconstructed: the porch's depth (K07's 0.95 m reveal, the drawing showing its back but not how far in), the door's leaf, transom and joinery (L-k01-1623-farwell-entrance-2728).

street_front_openings.note: Read through the drawing's camera (data/reference_views/house_1623_prairie/building_budget_front.json), at the front's 46 px/m: the principal storey's window is one broad round-arched light, its sill at about 2.1 m, its springing at about 3.4 m and its crown at about 4.4 m, about 1.8 m across inside a ring of long voussoirs about 0.5 m deep; under it a broad segmental basement light behind an iron grille, from grade to about 0.9 m. Built as K01's arched principal light at the drawing's 1.55 m centre (T-2777), its sill at 2.1 m and its crown at 4.4 m under a 0.35 m ring; T-2819 widens it to the drawing's 1.8 m (it had been narrowed to 1.6 m so its voussoir block stood 0.4 m inside the corner; at 1.8 m the block stands 0.3 m inside, past K01's 0.25 m), so it springs at 3.5 m, 0.1 m over the carved band's top as the drawn arch is stilted over it, on K06's wide sash with its head glazed as a lattice (window_kit). T-2818: under it the drawing's basement light, built as K06's broad segmental basement light, 1.8 m across from 0.1 m to its crown at 0.97 m, its head rising 0.11 m (a sixteenth of its span, the drawing's flat arc), centred 1.45 m from the north wall, 0.1 m north of the window over it (`offset_m`; the drawing draws it about 0.25 m north, between x 63 and 145, and 1.45 m is as far as its voussoirs stand 0.3 m inside the corner): through the camera its jambs land at x 68 and 150 and its crown at about y 647, against the drawn 63, 145 and 647, its sill within about 2 px. Over it a block of voussoirs 0.25 m deep radiating from the arc's centre, with a skewback at each end and a keystone to 1.25 m, where the drawing's radiating stones stop at about 1.3 m. T-2819: the window's head is glazed as the drawing's lattice, a grid of square lights 0.2 m apart (about eight across the drawn head) over the transom bar on the spring line; the bars' section is K06's muntin (reconstructed, L-k01-1623-farwell-entrance-2728).

street_front_dress.note: The rusticated base's coping at 1.0 m, over two courses of the Lemont stone (the rock-faced front above it is stone_front's, T-2728). T-2728: the drawing's iron. The stoop rises between iron rails, the K11 kit's stair rail as 1612's (T-2369): a newel at its head and one at its foot, a raked handrail, two balusters to a tread and a scroll at the foot; the drawing's newels are slim iron posts under flared caps, the kit's square ones. The basement light under the window stands behind an iron grille let into its reveal 0.05 m behind the face, as the drawing draws it (T-2818): eight close uprights from the sill to a bar at 0.57 m, a bar across them 0.25 m over the sill, and over the bar a band of six scrolls to the springing, each a flat bar curled into its centre and turned alternately, where the drawing draws a row of about six C-scrolls over its uprights at about 0.58-0.9 m and a bar across them at about 0.25 m. Read from the drawing: the rails, the grille's place, its band of scrolls and the number of them; reconstructed (the value's grade): every bar's count and section, and each scroll's curl (L-k01-1623-farwell-entrance-2728). T-2817: the landing's guard, which the drawing draws at the stoop's head running south along the landing before the porch's south jamb (x 277-335, v about 3.9-6.15 at the landing's edge), an ornamental panel at its south end (about x 302-327, v 5.45-6.0): built from the stoop rail's head newel to a newel at v 6.15, at the stoop rail's height, with its handrail, a foot bar and the rail's baluster pitch, and in the panel a lozenge of flat bar on a ring between two posts, where the drawing's ornament is too small to read (reconstructed, L-k01-1623-farwell-entrance-2728). The drawing's guard rail stands lower than the kit's 0.86 m over the landing (about 0.25-0.6 m, the plate's heights at the stoop's head being loose); it is built at the stoop rail's height, which a landing's guard needs. T-2819: the carved band at the arches' springing, which the drawing draws as a band of carving across the front on the north pier, between the arches and south of the porch's mouth, level with the window's transom, between y 534 and 556: through the solved camera (46 px/m at the front, its eye 1.6 m up at y 618) about 2.95-3.4 m, its top the drawn springing (y 535, the ticket's 3.4 m). Built as a dressed belt course from 2.95 to 3.4 m (`carved_band`), cut by the window's and the porch's openings, and on each run of it the oriel's frieze carving, a guilloche of interlaced rings 0.34 m across, where the drawing's carving is foliage too small to read (reconstructed, L-k01-1623-farwell-entrance-2728). Both arches spring a little over it (the window's at 3.6 m, the porch's at 3.525 m), their jambs rising past the band, as the drawing's arches are stilted over theirs.

boundary.note: T-3215: no boundary across the front. Treat & Foltz's 1886 drawing of the Farwell house (data/reference_views/house_1623_prairie/building_budget_front.json) draws the stoop climbing straight up from the walk between its iron rails and the low railed terrace beside it, and no fence, wall, coping or gate across the front yard. Carried to 1904 on that drawing alone (the house as designed, eighteen years before the scene; no later picture of the front is held), so INFERRED. The stoop's rails, newels and the terrace's railing are the house's own and stay as built. The lot's sides are parcel prairie_1623's street corners (data/street_grid/1904.json) in this frame, s -1.16 and 6.161.

yard.note: T-3215 (the owner, 2026-10-27). The drawing's stoop rises from the ground in front of the house with no fence before it, so the walk is laid in flags from the stoop's foot, its width (1.7 m), straight out to the inner edge of the public walk, 3.8 m before the street front; the lawn covers the rest of the front yard. The drawing hatches the ground and does not show a walk's line or material. RECONSTRUCTED: the walk's flags, their width and wear, the lawn and its bare strip are the K14 kit's (data/components/prairie_1904/k14_condition.json) aged from the phase's own year, as the kit's rule is; liberty L-k14-walks-1600-block-3215. T-3233: the lawn is the app's own ground (`lawn: none`), not the kit's turf sheet, which met the ground beside it in a straight line of another green; the yard's grass now runs on to the side yards' and the margin's with no seam.
